lines.text: Every building has one person who knows it by heart.
By 2036, 12.9 million people in Germany reach retirement age.
What they knew was never written down. Which extinguisher has the loose bracket. Which door is always locked.
So the new shift searches. Asks around. Writes it up later, if at all.
Maintenance software knows what. Location tracking knows roughly where. Nobody tells you, hands-free, where to go, and nobody keeps what you learned there.
Gisela plans her fire-extinguisher round on the laptop. The shortest order is computed on the building's own plans, and she sees what colleagues left at each stop.
Every fact comes from code, not from the language model. Areas, walls, floors, door widths, routes: computed on Synera's route model. The model only picks the tool and phrases the answer.
That's why all 145 benchmark answers are reproducible.
And it works on any building, even from the evacuation plan on the wall. This is the building we're standing in.
The knowledge stays in the building.
